question: Which countries license stablecoins, and what must back them?
answer: The library tracks 22 jurisdictions. Each card says who must license a stablecoin issuer there, what has to back the coin and what holders can claim, and which issuers are actually operating.

items.title: United States
kv: Who licenses

Entry may require an exact federal or state charter, stablecoin-issuer approval, money-transmission or trust authority, securities or commodities registration or scoped exemption, AML and sanctions controls, product or venue approval, and separate Federal Reserve account and service onboarding. The Federal Reserve proposed application procedures for Board-supervised issuers and specified state-qualified issuers; those procedures remain proposals and do not identify an approved applicant. The SEC order, OCC preliminary charter decisions, CFTC prerule review and TCH network plan operate at different gates; none establishes a generally operating firm or comprehensive regime.
What must back it

GENIUS payment stablecoins are private issuer liabilities backed by eligible reserve assets and a statutory redemption framework; the Act does not make them federally insured or government-guaranteed dollars. The Federal Reserve's proposed prudential rule would require covered issuers to maintain fair-value reserves at least equal to outstanding issuance at all times, calculate the position daily as of 5 p.m., remediate deficiencies within 24 hours, and meet a proposed two-business-day redemption standard. A tokenized bank deposit remains a bank-deposit claim. A DTC token is a controlled representation inside DTC's entitlement architecture rather than native bearer title to the underlying security. OUSD is a Bridge-issued stablecoin whose launch page names BlackRock, Lead Bank and BNY reserve roles; the first promised monthly attestation had not yet been published.
Who is operating

The existing owners identify the Federal Reserve and Reserve Banks, Treasury, SEC, CFTC, OCC, FDIC, NCUA, FinCEN, OFAC, DTC and DTCC alongside exact issuers, custodians, banks, exchanges, wallets, processors and networks. The September OCC decisions add proposed Agora and Catena trust-bank legal persons at the preliminary conditional charter stage. Bridge Building Inc. is the identified OUSD issuer within the Bridge/Stripe group; BlackRock, Lead Bank and BNY have stated reserve roles; Coinbase, Mastercard/BVNK, Stripe and Visa are distribution or integration paths rather than the token debtor. The Clearing House and Quant are future network operator and technology-provider roles, not deposit issuers for each member bank. The deeper Crypto Infrastructure Hub owns the entity and relationship graph.

items.title: United Kingdom
kv: Who licenses

MLR registration and financial-promotion compliance are current gates. The FCA's new-regime authorization gateway opened at 09:00 on 30 September 2026 and is scheduled to close at 23:59 on 28 February 2027, with the broader regime expected to commence 25 October 2027. Existing FSMA firms generally apply to vary permission; other firms apply for authorization. Timely applicants may rely on the applicable saving provision while pending, whereas late applicants are limited to transition or runoff and may not enter new contracts.
What must back it

Issuer, custody and backing questions are product-specific. Platform custody can combine blockchain state, internal entitlement records, key control and subcustody; lending can replace a proprietary asset position with a contractual return claim.
Who is operating

The FCA evidence identifies consumer-facing platforms, protocols, issuers, trading venues, intermediaries, principal traders, custodians, banks, payment firms, lenders and staking providers as roles. Survey brand names do not establish the exact contracting or regulated legal entity.

items.title: Japan
kv: Who licenses

At cutoff the FSA listed 27 cryptoasset exchange providers and two electronic-payment-instrument service providers. SBI VC Trade is registered for USDC, RLUSD and JPYSC; Coincheck's 27 August registration covers USDC. JPYSC access and direct redemption require identity, legality, wallet and bank-account checks; bank-issued tokenized deposits remain issuer and customer specific.
What must back it

JPYSC is a specified-trust beneficiary claim backed by trust assets and is neither legal tender, a bank deposit nor deposit-insured. The 30 June snapshot disclosed ¥10,008,294,794 issued and ¥10,008,304,794 in the trust's deposit account. When a customer lends JPYSC to SBI VC Trade, that customer instead holds an unsecured consumption-loan repayment claim outside customer-asset segregation. DCJPY is an issuing-bank deposit backed by the bank's balance sheet. A future retail CBDC or tokenized BOJ current-account balance would be a BOJ claim only if legally and operationally issued.
Who is operating

The national record identifies the FSA, BOJ, MOF, DICJ, BOJ-NET, Zengin-Net, JSCC, SBI Shinsei Trust Bank, SBI VC Trade, Coincheck, DeCurret DCP, GMO Aozora Net Bank, TradeWaltz, the three megabank groups and participating banking groups in distinct roles. XRP Asia now lists Tokyo as a community node. It is a regional ecosystem-support body, not SBI Ripple Asia, a Japanese regulated provider or a bank settlement operator.

items.title: South Korea
kv: Who licenses

The 26 surveyed reporting providers comprised 17 exchanges and 9 custody/wallet businesses; 28 VASPs were notified and two did not submit the survey. Revised entry and controlling-shareholder review took effect on 20 August, while other AML provisions follow a later clock. Proposed security-token issuer account managers need KRW 4 billion equity, specified staff and a KSD-screened shared ledger.
What must back it

USDT is an issuer-linked stablecoin claim whose direct redemption depends on issuer terms and custody; Project Hangang tokens are commercial-bank deposit claims on participating banks and were described as deposit-protected. A future public KRW stablecoin's issuer, reserves and redemption constitution were unresolved.
Who is operating

FSC identifies KB Kookmin, Shinhan, Woori, Hana, NH NongHyup, IBK and Busan Bank as continuing Hangang banks and Kyongnam and iM Bank as newly designated for Phase II. KB separately issued a USD 100 million digital bond through HSBC Orion linked to HKMA CMU and announced a Kinexys corporate USD route. XRP Asia now lists Seoul as a community node, while the official XRP Seoul program separately lists Ripple, Kbank, Kyobo Securities, Woori Bank and JB Bank on a bank panel. Program co-presence does not create an XRP Asia contract or XRPL deployment. Upbit, KRX, KSD and settlement banks occupy different exchange and infrastructure roles.

items.title: Indonesia
kv: Who licenses

OJK licensing applies separately to exchanges, clearing/settlement institutions, custodians and dealers; each exchange controls its Digital Financial Asset List. PADK 3/2026 supplies current reporting procedures. Similar business models may seek registration after a sandbox model passes, but passage is not registration. Segregated consumer accounts may be opened only at an OJK-licensed commercial bank.
What must back it

Rupiah bank and e-money balances remain claims on their exact providers; segregated crypto customer funds sit as commercial-bank deposits under the market arrangement; cryptoasset ownership and custody run through dealer/custodian records; future Digital Rupiah would be a BI claim. IDRP's reserve owner, eligible assets, bank, attestation, redemption and insolvency terms were not established by the sandbox result.
Who is operating

Named crypto actors include exchanges CFX and ICEX, licensed dealer PT Indonesia Digital Exchange, denied applicant PT Gerbang Aset Digital and sandbox participant PT Adhyoka Berkah Maju/IDRP. Major payment banks include Bank Mandiri, BRI, BNI, BCA and BSI. The public aggregate confirms two clearing institutions and two custodians but the normalized card still requires a current exact-name roster for every entity.

items.title: European Union
kv: Who licenses

MiCA issuer and CASP authorization, national authority action, electronic-money or banking status, DLT-infrastructure authorization, whitepaper notification, Eurosystem eligibility, participant onboarding and CSD/TARGET access are separate gates. The maximum transitional period ended by 1 July 2026. ESMA warns that a whitepaper in its interim register is not authority approval. Qivalis applied to De Nederlandsche Bank but remained outside the authorization gate.
What must back it

At the observed 1 October disclosure EUR CoinVertible had €167,013,839.02 in circulation with reserves stated as 100 percent at Société Générale; USD CoinVertible had $12,546,441 in circulation with reserves stated as 87.67 percent at BNY and 12.33 percent at Société Générale. SG-FORGE describes one-for-one redemption, segregated collateral and daily reserve composition. These are issuer disclosures about the issuer's EMT liabilities and assets. BBVA-custodied bitcoin and ether are customer cryptoassets, and Qivalis's one-for-one backing remains a future design.
Who is operating

Named actors include SG-FORGE as a live EMT issuer and regulated service entity; BBVA Spain as a bank crypto-service provider; Deutsche Bank, Lloyds, CaixaBank and the Eurosystem in a Project Agorá real-value route; EIB, Clearstream, DekaBank, Eurex Clearing and Bundesbank in the completed DLT-collateral circuit; and 37 banks in the pre-authorization Qivalis consortium. UniCredit reports tokenized-asset transactions, while Intesa's disclosed crypto and token plans remain strategic.

items.title: Singapore
kv: Who licenses

Gates can include a named PSA licence or exemption and activity, SFA/FAA offer and intermediary permissions, FSMA Part 9 licensing with prescribed S$250,000 financial resources, MAS management approval, AML/CFT and technology-risk controls, customer-asset safeguarding, designated-system admission, and project-specific testnet eligibility. The dedicated stablecoin gate remains proposed legislation.
What must back it

Licensed DPT providers must apply trust, safeguarding and recordkeeping rules to customer assets. The future MAS-SCS model would add one-for-one reserves, capital, par redemption, disclosure, stress testing and wind-down requirements, but is not yet an operating issuer regime. The Swift-ledger transactions recorded separate DBS, OCBC and UOB tokenized-deposit obligations on each bank's infrastructure. Crypto in DBS custody, DBS structured notes, OCBC commercial paper and GOLDX fund tokens are different customer assets or securities; wholesale CBDC and MEPS+ balances are MAS liabilities for bounded eligible participants.
Who is operating

The MAS Directory returned 38 DPT-service Major Payment Institution entities on 15 September, including DBS Vickers and named specialist firms. Separate bank-primary records establish DBS, OCBC and UOB as live tokenized-deposit transaction participants; HSBC Singapore and Standard Chartered Singapore operate corporate tokenized-deposit services. XRP Asia Ltd now identifies Singapore as its organizational home and regional XRPL community base, while Ripple Markets APAC remains the separately licensed Ripple legal person. DBS Bank, DBS Vickers, DBS Digital Exchange and DBS Trustee occupy different bank, service, exchange and trust roles. OCBC, Lion Global Investors and DigiFT perform distinct functions in GOLDX.

items.title: Australia
kv: Who licenses

A business may need AUSTRAC enrolment and VASP registration, an AFSL or authorization under current law, market or clearing and settlement authority, APRA-regulated bank status, or later DAP and TCP authorisations. ASIC's conditional no-action deadline was extended to 30 September 2026. RITS and ESA access are separate from product and platform licensing.
What must back it

Project Acacia deliberately tested different money claims: existing ESA balances, a pilot RBA wholesale CBDC, tokenised commercial-bank deposits and stablecoins. A tokenised deposit remains a bank liability; a digitally native tokenised reserve would be an RBA liability if issued; a digital-twin reserve would represent segregated ESA balances. The future DAF platform contract does not itself make an underlying token sovereign or guaranteed.
Who is operating

ANZ, BHP, Citi and Swift are named in the live September USD route. Project Acacia separately identifies ANZ, CBA, NAB and Westpac across proof, working-group and collaboration roles: ANZ led bond and trade-payable PoCs; CBA led an intraday-repo PoC; Westpac led a PayTo/tokenized-term-deposit PoC; NAB and all four banks joined the Deposit Token Working Group. AP+, Austraclear, ASX, HQLAX, Kinexys and several private-money issuers own different infrastructure and settlement records.

items.title: New Zealand
kv: Who licenses

Depending on the activity, gates can include FSPR registration, retail DRS membership, FMC disclosure and governance, a specified FMA or RBNZ licence, DIA-supervised AML/CFT compliance, CARF reporting status, ESAS account approval or NZClear participation. NZDD additionally depends on ECDD maintaining reserve sufficiency and public monthly verification, obtaining annual independent verification, and satisfying account-holder eligibility and compliance terms. The designation switches off during a defined period of non-compliance until remedy. FSPR registration generally involves limited checks and does not itself confer a licence.
What must back it

The NZDD designation requires ECDD to hold NZD at least equal to the underlying currency amount of NZDD in circulation, as trustee on bare trust for holders, in a trust account whose assets are call debt securities issued by registered banks. Eligible account holders may return tokens and require NZD delivery, subject to commercially reasonable restrictions. The designation does not state that the token holder is the registered bank's depositor or that NZDD is DCS protected; only eligible covered deposits receive DCS compensation. Digital Cash would be an RBNZ-issued government-backed NZD liability if approved, while ESAS balances already are central-bank money for approved participants.
Who is operating

The primary record identifies ECDD Holdings Limited as NZDD issuer, the FMA as designation maker and New Zealand registered banks as the permissible reserve-account issuers without naming the current reserve bank. RBNZ identifies ANZ New Zealand, ASB, BNZ and Westpac New Zealand as the four D-SIBs; RBNZ's 2026 stress-test description says those four account for 84 percent of lending, while ANZ, ASB, BNZ, Kiwibank and Westpac together accounted for 91 percent in the 2025 industry test. A bounded current bank-primary search located conventional deposits, open-banking payments, digital identity and risk statements, but no New Zealand-bank stablecoin, transferable deposit token, customer crypto custody or tokenised settlement launch.

sources.label: Financial Markets Conduct (ECDD Holdings Limited Stablecoin) Designation Notice 2026

items.title: Brazil
kv: Who licenses

New specialist providers require BCB authorization before operation. Qualifying legacy providers may operate only through the formal transition and authorization process. Existing BCB-regulated institutions face activity-specific communication and waiting rules. Resolution 589 moved the date after which BCB-authorized institutions must not enable virtual-asset operations with non-authorized provider counterparties to 6 November 2026; the amended wording and BCB transition process must be read together rather than treating continuing operation as a final approval. CVM, STR, SPI, Pix, Selic and Drex retain separate legal-person, product, account, technical, liquidity or pilot-participation gates.
What must back it

For fiat-referenced virtual assets offered by in-country providers, Resolution 520 requires review and disclosure of issuer, fiat or same-sovereign public-debt reserves, custody, audited material and available redemption or reserve-claim mechanisms, and bars algorithmically controlled reserves. These remain private issuer and reserve claims. Drex pilot units are simulated; STR and SPI balances are central-bank money; a tokenised security carries its own underlying legal right. In the CSD BR project, the permissioned XRPL MPT is a complementary representation of selected deposited fund shares, while CSD BR's system remains the official record.
Who is operating

BCB's March 2026 prudential segmentation places BB, Bradesco, BTG Pactual, Caixa, Itaú and Santander in S1. Their verified digital-asset states differ: Itaú offers app-based BTC, ETH and USDC trading with bank custody; BTG offers crypto trading/custody, markets BTG Dol and is the fund manager named in the CSD BR mirror; Banco do Brasil distributes a crypto-exposure fund and, with Caixa and cooperatives, signed the September mortgage-tokenization development agreement; Caixa, Bradesco and Santander have Drex or tokenization pilot/development evidence but no reviewed public token-money launch. Nubank, though not S1, is a material retail intermediary whose current terms cover buy, sell, swap, custody and selected on-chain transfers. A cutoff SPSAV cohort by CNPJ and final/in-process state remains unavailable.

items.title: Argentina
kv: Who licenses

Covered providers must register before operating and identify the exact categories. Foreign providers face local-structure and nexus tests. Minimum net worth is US$150,000 for Categories 1, 2 and 4, US$75,000 for Category 3 and US$35,000 for Category 5, with a specified 50% reduction below US$2.5 million rolling transaction/custody thresholds. AML registration, governance, custody, systems, audit and reporting requirements apply separately.
What must back it

Category 4 PSAVs must publish proof of reserves, separate customer virtual assets and fiat from own property, keep customer virtual assets outside PSAV assets and refrain from own-account use. No reviewed official source created a dedicated stablecoin issuer reserve, direct par-redemption, recognized-token or sovereign-guarantee regime. In the tokenised-securities sandbox, the traditional authorized security and its ADCVN deposit remain behind the digital representation.
Who is operating

CNV publishes a JavaScript-backed PSAV register and accepts registrations/cancellations through TAD. The reviewed static surface did not yield a reliable cutoff export of exact legal persons, categories, suspensions and cancellations; a crawler's zero result is not treated as the cohort count. The BCRA's current entity list and major-private-bank group supply the bank perimeter, while its present crypto page retains the operating restriction. Banco Nacion, Galicia, Santander Argentina, BBVA Argentina and Banco Macro were reviewed as the major-bank layer. Galicia's own 2022 disclosure records a short-lived purchase, sale and custody launch before the BCRA restriction; Banco Nacion's 25 September 2026 statement describes capability-building pending permission; Santander's Agrotoken work reached a pilot; no current direct crypto trading, custody, deposit token or bank-issued stablecoin was verified at those five institutions.

items.title: South Africa
kv: Who licenses

A covered provider must join the exact legal person and service to an FSCA FSP authorization or representative status, fit-and-proper and conduct duties, FIC Item 22 registration and AML controls. Banking/payment access and any FinSurv permission or individual allowance remain additional gates.
What must back it

Crypto is not SARB-issued, backed or guaranteed, and no dedicated prudential stablecoin-issuer licence was located. ZARU is a current private issuer structure: Loop South Africa, trading as BlockTower, is the issuer and FSP; Standard Bank holds cash and deposit reserves and provides securities custody; Sanlam Investment Management holds or manages the money-market portion; and Moore performs monthly agreed-upon procedures. The 31 July snapshot reported R23.314 million of cash and bank deposits plus R30.403 million of money-market funds against 52.946 million ZARU. Direct mint and redemption are limited by the whitepaper to verified institutional clients; retail or other holders use authorized partners. The report says Loop is the bank account holder and fund investor, so a token holder has an issuer redemption claim rather than a bank deposit in their own name. Khokha 2 wCBDC and bank tokens were experimental liabilities inside a proof of concept.
Who is operating

SARB reported 310 FSCA-licensed CASPs at 31 March 2026. Its Tether scale figure names Luno, VALR and AltCoinTrader only as the three measured platforms. SARB currently designates Absa, Standard Bank, FirstRand, Nedbank, Investec and Capitec as systemically important banks. In that bank layer, Standard Bank provides ZARU reserve banking and securities custody and operates Aroko; Absa markets institutional digital-asset custody; Nedbank has announced a conditional Crypto.com ZAR/USDC rollout; Absa, FirstRand, Nedbank and Standard Bank were active Khokha 2 participants; Investec participated in the broader project work and describes sandboxed capability; Capitec supplies risk warnings but no reviewed digital-asset product. FSCA publishes regulated-entity search surfaces, but this pass did not establish a cutoff export joining every legal person, service category, condition, suspension and active domain.

sources.label: SARB Financial Surveillance and crypto FAQ

items.title: Nigeria
kv: Who licenses

Entry depends on asset and activity classification, exact SEC or CBN perimeter, legal-person registration or scoped incubation, category-specific capital, AML/CFT/CPF and consumer safeguards, bank due diligence, CBN authorization for a designated VASP settlement account, tax registration and any additional payment, FX or data permissions.
What must back it

eNaira is direct CBN liability and legal tender. cNGN is a private WrappedCBDC liability under conditional SEC ARIP AIP. Current issuer terms promise minting only against naira deposits and one-to-one redemption after token burn for verified users, but say retail holders are not WrappedCBDC customers and the token is neither government-backed nor deposit-insured. The issuer says reserves sit in approved commercial banks but does not name the exact account banks or publish a cutoff reserve report on the reviewed surface. An IMF report reproduced about 66 million cNGN across roughly 20 addresses from an issuer-origin source. No reviewed final instrument established a general private-stablecoin issuer licence joining reserve composition, segregated custody, attestation, direct holder claim, run management and insolvency. Sandbox application requirements test such controls but do not certify an issuer or coin.
Who is operating

The SEC current directory lists Busha Digital Limited and Quidax Technologies Limited in ARIP. SEC added Bitbarter, Luno Fintech Nigeria, GetEquity, Koinkoin, WrappedCBDC, Trovotech and Blockvault Custodian in July, then Pisi Payments, BC Access Nigeria and Yellow Card in August, all under conditional AIP rather than final licences. The directory still displays WrappedCBDC's older cNGN Regulatory Incubation period ending 28 August 2025, but SEC's 2 July release is the later current status. CBN's latest located stability report says five banks were D-SIBs at December 2024 without naming them. The bank overlay therefore reviews large national groups without claiming a current official five-name roster: Access has live eNaira account integration and a production PAPSS service; FirstBank publishes eNaira customer guidance; no direct private-crypto trading, custody or bank-issued stablecoin was verified at Access, FirstBank, UBA, Zenith or GTBank.

sources.label: Presidential Executive Order on Virtual Assets Coordination

items.title: Kenya
kv: Who licenses

Entry turns on the exact activity and regulator, complete application and due diligence, fit-and-proper and source-of-funds review, category capital and liquidity, local bank accounts, AML/CFT/CPF, cybersecurity, consumer and continuity controls, cross-border disclosure, tax duties and any separate FX authorization. The rules apply to foreign providers targeting Kenyan consumers or deriving Kenyan economic benefit.
What must back it

The final rules require a stablecoin holder claim against the issuer, issuance and redemption at par, two-working-day redemption, full reserve backing, permitted short-duration assets, legal segregation and insolvency remoteness, CBK-approved custody, at least 30% of received funds in segregated Kenyan trust accounts, quarterly stress tests and reserve audits. No named licensed issuer, coin, reserve pool, audit or redemption series was established.
Who is operating

CBK's 10 August 2026 PSP directory names Safaricom PLC, Airtel Money Kenya Limited and other legal persons for conventional payment services; Safaricom is authorized to issue, process, store, send and facilitate mobile-money payments. The November 2025 CBK/CMA notice said no VASP was then licensed. No post-regulations cutoff export joining a VASP legal person to category, conditions and commencement was located. For the bank overlay, CBK's 2025 supervision report defines an eight-bank Large peer group—KCB Bank Kenya, Equity Bank Kenya, Co-operative Bank of Kenya, Absa Bank Kenya, NCBA Bank Kenya, Stanbic Bank Kenya, I&M Bank and Diamond Trust Bank Kenya. Their own current materials prove different preparation states but no locally scoped bank-issued stablecoin, direct retail crypto dealing or production crypto-custody launch: KCB maps a possible future banking-partner role; Co-op has a risk/compliance assessment underway; Stanbic identifies possible partnership, payment-rail and custody implications; Absa Kenya is building virtual-asset custody capacity; NCBA and I&M publish market research; Equity and DTB disclose digital-banking transformation without a named crypto product.

items.title: Ghana
kv: Who licenses

Act 1154 requires registration or licensing by the regulator assigned to the activity. Bank of Ghana's current interface still said that its general application and fee pages would be available by end-Q3 2026, but neither page was live at the 1 October cutoff. SEC sandbox entry requires a complete application, risk and operational evidence, written conditioned approval and any customer or asset safeguards imposed; ninety days is not automatic approval, and foreign VASP applicants need at least 30% local participation plus an approved Ghana presence.
What must back it

Stablecoin issuance is a regulated activity, but virtual assets are not cedi, government-guaranteed, deposit-insured or covered by a statutory compensation fund. SEC may impose safeguarding, segregation, escrow, custody, trust, insurance, compensation and recovery controls in a sandbox. Ghana Gold Board is testing a gold real-world-asset custody role and Africoin Ghana a gold-tokenisation activity in the sandbox, while GoldBod separately says a fractional-ownership tokenisation programme is planned for 2027. Its US$75 million commercial-bank financing and self-funded gold aggregation are conventional funding and inventory arrangements, not token reserves. No general final stablecoin holder-claim, reserve, attestation, par-redemption or insolvency regime was established.
Who is operating

SEC's 19 August 2026 notice joins 20 legal persons to approved pilot activities, including Africoin Ghana, Vaulta Digital Assets, GFX Brokers, One Africa Securities, Wewire Ghana, Yellow Card Ghana, Hyro Exchange, Whitebit Ghana, Koinkoin Ghana, Ghana Commodities Exchange, Ghana Gold Board and eight other providers. No cutoff notice proving a participant's transition to a full activity licence was located. Ghana has not yet published a named D-SIB roster: Bank of Ghana says the framework is being designed for a 2026-2028 implementation roadmap. The major-bank overlay therefore uses the latest explicit asset-ranked population—Ecobank Ghana, GCB, Stanbic Ghana, Absa Ghana, Fidelity Bank and Zenith Bank—and finds no locally scoped crypto launch among them. GCB operates conventional G-Money; Fidelity participated in the concluded eCedi pilot; Stanbic published recommendations; Absa's live custody and licences remain conventional.

sources.label: Securities Industry Regulatory Sandbox Licensing Guidelines 2026
Frequently Asked Questions — Virtual Asset Service Providers Act

items.title: Hong Kong
kv: Who licenses

A centralised platform operating in Hong Kong or actively marketing to Hong Kong investors requires SFC licensing. Regulated specified-stablecoin activity requires HKMA licensing and ongoing satisfaction of statutory minimum criteria. The live registers, not an application, deemed state, sandbox participation, consultation or marketing claim, establish licensed entry.
What must back it

A specified-stablecoin holder has a par-redemption right, ordinarily within one business day after a valid request. Reserve assets must support outstanding obligations, be segregated and protected through effective trust arrangements; insolvency rights include pro-rata reserve-pool disposal and a shortfall claim against the issuer. HKDAP's whitepaper identifies Anchorpoint as debtor, Ethereum as its initial chain, Standard Chartered Hong Kong as reserve manager and intended custodian, Standard Chartered Trustee as trustee for non-digital reserve assets, and a wholesale authorised-distributor model. At 23 September Anchorpoint's weekly unaudited statement reported HK$1,006,890 in circulation and HK$2,110,045 of reserves, of which HK$1.1 million was issuer-funded overcollateralisation. Independent attestations had not begun. HSBC says RedCoin will be fully backed by segregated liquid assets and redeemable one-for-one, but the product remained future-tense.
Who is operating

The SFC list names 13 formally licensed VATP legal persons. HKMA's live register names Anchorpoint Financial Limited (FRS01) and The Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited (FRS02). Anchorpoint is now an operating issuer in Beta Access, with OSL, HashKey, Standard Chartered Hong Kong, Finloop and Yunfeng Financial among named early distributors; HSBC's RedCoin remains pre-launch. EnsembleTX names seven tokenised-deposit banks. The current D-SIB roster names HSBC, BOCHK, Standard Chartered Hong Kong, Hang Seng and ICBC Asia; only the exact legal person's locally evidenced role is attributed.

Explanatory Note on Licensing of Stablecoin Issuers

items.title: China
kv: Who licenses

There is no general mainland VASP licensing lane. Bank-wallet e-CNY requires PBOC operator approval, central-system connection, completed business/technical preparation and customer go-live; nonbank service adds payment-institution, guarantee-fund and AML requirements. CBETS, mBridge/Jisr, CIPS and Payment Connect each require their own participant, account, liquidity, FX and use-case admissions.
What must back it

A commercial-bank e-CNY wallet is an account-based liability of that bank, may earn interest, enters its reserve base and receives deposit-equivalent insurance treatment. A nonbank wallet is the provider's liability backed by 100% e-CNY guarantee funds. Deposit insurance currently pays covered principal and interest up to CNY 500,000 per depositor aggregated at one insured institution, with excess claims in liquidation. Private virtual-currency losses may be self-borne when the civil act violates public order, while criminal tracing and restitution remain separate.
Who is operating

PBOC had approved 30 bank-class e-CNY operators by 18 August 2026: the six large state-owned banks, China Merchants Bank, Industrial Bank, MYbank, WeBank, 12 banks added in April and eight added in August. The six large banks—ICBC, ABC, BOC, CCB, Bank of Communications and PSBC—also appear in the 2025 domestic systemically important bank list. New cohorts must finish preparation before service. Bank-specific evidence establishes that all six original operators have customer wallet or e-CNY application states, while BOC, ICBC, CCB, BoCom and PSBC disclose specific cross-border or smart-contract receipts. Digital RMB operating centers own domestic/international infrastructure; CBETS names 26 initial direct participants and BOC completed the first batch of Singapore retail transactions. CIPS reported 210 direct and 1,619 indirect participants at June 2026.

Digital renminbi enters the deposit-money 2.0 framework

items.title: United Arab Emirates
kv: Who licenses

Payment-token issuance requires a CBUAE licence; conversion and foreign-token custody may require CBUAE non-objection on top of SCA or local VASP status. VARA in-principle approval cannot operate or serve clients. DIFC and ADGM require their own DFSA or FSRA authorisation. Register inclusion and exact activity scope establish entry, not an application, marketing claim or group-company licence.
What must back it

Payment-token holders have a par-redemption right without delay and no later than the same time on the next business day unless CBUAE permits otherwise. The default reserve is 100% same-currency cash in segregated escrow; a bank-owned issuer may hold at least 50% cash and the remainder in short-duration UAE government bonds or CBUAE M-bills. Daily reconciliation/reporting, monthly external audit and an insolvency claim against the reserve are required. Issuer-specific current balances and redemption performance remain open.
Who is operating

The live CBUAE register names AED StableCoin L.L.C - S.P.C, Zand Trust L.L.C S.O.C and AEDC Stable Coin-L.L.C as Dirham Payment Token Issuance legal persons and AEDC Stable Coin Network And Distribution - L.L.C in conversion/custody and payment-service categories. VARA's cutoff register shows 56 active fully licensed VASPs in Dubai outside DIFC. AE Coin, AEDZ and DDSC have named product evidence. CBUAE's latest explicit public D-SIB population is FAB, Emirates NBD, ADCB and DIB; Zand is reviewed separately because its trust company is a registered issuer. Other federal and financial-free-zone rosters still need a joined cutoff export.

items.title: Switzerland
kv: Who licenses

Professional AML-covered intermediaries require direct supervision or recognised-SRO membership. Current fintech authorisation covers up to CHF 100 million of public deposits or collective cryptobased-asset custody if assets are neither invested nor interest-bearing; larger or invested deposits enter the banking perimeter. Securities, funds and FMIs have distinct gates. DLT trading facilities require FINMA authorisation before operation.
What must back it

FINMA says stablecoin holders generally hold an at-any-time payment claim against the issuer; classification normally follows public-deposit or collective-investment law depending on whose account and risk the backing is managed for. A bank default guarantee can remove funds from the deposit definition but carries conditions and residual issuer, holder and guarantor risks. The sandbox describes CHFD as 1:1 CHF-linked but does not publish the complete debtor, reserve, guarantee, redemption, attestation or insolvency chain. The participating banks are not automatically co-issuers. Helvetia wCBDC is an SNB liability; commercial deposits and custodied cryptoassets follow different protection paths.
Who is operating

FINMA's current material names UBS, Raiffeisen Group, Zürcher Kantonalbank and PostFinance as systemically important. The authorised-institutions list separately names AMINA Bank AG and Sygnum Bank AG as banks and Crypto Finance AG and Taurus SA as securities firms. All four systemic groups participate in the controlled CHFD sandbox, while customer-product states differ: ZKB provides direct bitcoin/ether custody and an interbank service; PostFinance offers 22-asset trading, custody and ETH staking with Sygnum; UBS operates tokenised-asset workflows but its cited service page says it has no active crypto offering; and no broader Raiffeisen customer crypto launch was verified. SIX operates regulated digital-securities CSD infrastructure; BX Digital is the sole listed DLT trading facility. Nine banks are currently eligible for Helvetia wCBDC, but eligibility does not establish usage by each bank.

items.title: France
kv: Who licenses

France-established CASPs pass through the AMF; passported EU providers rely on home authorisation and notification; EMT issuers require ACPR-supervised credit-institution or EMI status; TARGET and securities settlement require separate participant, account, CSD and system admission.
What must back it

EMT holders have at-par private claims on the exact issuer, supported by MiCA safeguarding and recovery/redemption duties. Circle discloses segregated EURC reserves; SG-FORGE discloses segregated collateral for EURCV and USDCV. CACEIS Bank's EURXT white paper makes CACEIS Bank the debtor, permits up to 70% of the reserve in highly liquid instruments and gives identified holders an at-par redemption process. The issuer website's statement that reserves consist entirely of central-bank cash is not fully reconciled with that white-paper permission and the current numerical reserve fields were not machine-readable at cutoff. BNP's ETNs are issuer securities, BPCE/Hexarq holdings are customer cryptoassets and Qivalis remains a future claim. Bank deposits, securities and central-bank money retain separate debtors and protection paths.
Who is operating

ACPR's six-principal-group comparison identifies BNP Paribas, Société Générale, Groupe Crédit Agricole, Groupe BPCE, Groupe Crédit Mutuel and La Banque Postale; the first four were 2024 G-SIBs. Exact operating legal persons differ inside those groups. Société Générale-FORGE issues EURCV and USDCV and is an EMI, investment firm and CASP. CACEIS Bank, the Crédit Agricole asset-servicing bank, is a notified credit-institution CASP and issues EURXT. Hexarq SAS, a BPCE subsidiary, is the licensed retail CASP. BNP Paribas' French commercial bank distributes securities-based crypto exposure while its asset-management, Securities Services and AssetFoundry units performed the tokenised-fund experiment. Banque Fédérative du Crédit Mutuel is a Qivalis member, not the proposed issuer. Circle France remains a separate non-major-bank EMT issuer.

items.title: Canada
kv: Who licenses

Entry can require FINTRAC MSB status, Bank of Canada PSP registration, province-specific securities decisions, CIRO membership, issuer undertakings, system membership and settlement accounts. Stablecoin Act registration awaits commencement and regulations.
What must back it

Current VRCAs remain private risky assets or platform contracts without regulated-deposit protection. A tokenised deposit would be a liability of its issuing bank and is not automatically a common six-bank coin; the announcement disclosed neither deposit-insurance treatment nor a common backing or loss-sharing structure. RPAA safeguarding protects qualifying end-user funds through trust or segregation plus insurance/guarantee. The future Stablecoin Act would require one-for-one qualifying reserves and at-par redemption for covered non-financial issuers but is not in force. USDC remains a claim on its exact issuer.
Who is operating

OSFI identifies Bank of Montreal, Bank of Nova Scotia, Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce, National Bank of Canada, Royal Bank of Canada and Toronto-Dominion Bank as domestic systemically important banks; RBC and TD are also global systemically important banks. All six are parties to the September tokenised-deposit exploration. Separately, CSA lists named platform legal persons in heterogeneous national and province-limited states; FINTRAC and Bank of Canada verify Tazapay Canada Corp.; and the Netcoins decision names Netcoins Inc. plus its operating jurisdictions.

items.title: Rwanda
kv: Who licenses

Article 10 requires a legal entity incorporated or registered in Rwanda with local presence, beneficial-owner disclosure, fit governance, regulatory capital and AML controls; regulations must prescribe procedures and capital. As of the cutoff, CMA's regulations page did not list a virtual-asset implementing regulation, its application page did not offer a VASP route, and its licensee page showed no VASP or approved issuer category. A June CMA procurement for virtual-asset consultancy indicates implementation work, not a licence window. Payment services still require the exact NBR licence, while Ghana passporting requires home permission, a Letter of No Objection and joint governance.
What must back it

Article 19 requires an approved stablecoin to be 100% collateralized at all times, bars lending reserve assets for yield, requires independent-auditor confirmation of liquidity for reasonable and timely redemption, verification means, a licensed professional custodian, regular audits and segregation from issuer and creditor assets for insolvency. Further regulations may still determine reserve-investment conditions. E-money remains a separately regulated redeemable issuer claim backed by at least equivalent authorized currency and safeguarded through trust or equivalent mechanisms; bank deposits remain bank liabilities subject to the DGF statute.
Who is operating

NBR's supervised-bank list names nine commercial banks—Bank of Kigali, BPR Bank Rwanda, I&M Bank Rwanda, GT Bank, Ecobank Rwanda, Access Bank Rwanda, Equity Bank Rwanda, BOA Rwanda and NCBA Rwanda—plus BRD and ZIGAMA CSS. NBR says five unnamed D-SIBs held 75.6% of banking assets at December 2024, so this record does not invent a name-to-D-SIB mapping. Bank of Kigali, BPR, I&M, Equity, Ecobank and Access form the bank operating sample. CMA separately lists Bank of Kigali, BPR and I&M as traditional capital-market custodians, not virtual-asset custodians. The current CMA roster names no VASP, stablecoin issuer or approved virtual-asset product. NBR's November 2025 list names 42 conventional PSP entities; the Ghana-Rwanda pilot's four firms remain unnamed.

catalog_context.title: Crypto around the world: many licenses, no proven cross-border use
catalog_context.answer: Across 22 jurisdictions, we found no verified cross-border payment route that depends on crypto from end to end. The token layer still settles through ordinary banks and national payment systems.
